related_questions.question: What are the new rules for travel to the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: For travelers to the UK, the main new rule is the requirement for an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for those who don't need a visa. This applies to many nationalities, including US, Canadian, and EU citizens, for short visits (up to six months) for tourism, business, or family visits. The ETA is similar to the US ESTA and must be obtained before travel.
snippet_highlighted_words: the requirement for an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for those who don't need a visa

list.title: Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA):
list.snippet: Most travelers, including US, Canadian, and EU citizens, will need an ETA for short visits to the UK.

list.title: ETA Requirements:
list.snippet: The ETA is a digital authorization, similar to the US ESTA, and must be obtained before travel.

list.title: Passport Validity:
list.snippet: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in the UK.

list.title: Visa Requirements:
list.snippet: If you need a visa for your trip, you will not need an ETA. The ETA is for those who don't need a visa.

list.title: Application:
list.snippet: You can apply for the ETA online, typically through a mobile app, and applications can take up to 72 hours for processing.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: The ETA fee is currently £10 (about $13), but will increase to £16 (about $20) on April 9, 2025.

list.title: No COVID-19 Restrictions:
list.snippet: There are no COVID-19 related restrictions for travel to the UK.

list.title: Official Information:
list.snippet: For the most up-to-date and accurate information, consult the official UK government website.
